original_abstract.text: In expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts serving, a layer finishes only when the most loaded GPU of its group does. Token routing shifts at every decode step and concentrates on a few experts, so most of the group's reserved GPU time waits on stragglers. Recovering that time means re-deciding, at every layer of every decode step, how each replicated expert's tokens divide between its copies. The exact linear-program solvers that make this decision optimally take longer than many of the layers they serve, and their working set outgrows GPU shared memory at deployment scale. We introduce Relief, a bidirectional pairwise relaxation that makes the linear program unnecessary, coming within a fraction of a point of the per-step optimum in a few passes of integer halving over the token counts. We build and measure three deployments, CUDA kernels on the serving GPU, the same verified engine on an FPGA over PCIe, and a fixed-function block beside the accelerator. On decode routing from three open MoE families, Relief holds the balance near the per-step optimum at every group size and layer time measured. Scored as effective utilization relative to that optimum, the kernel alone matches or exceeds every deployable scheme at every group size, from the hundred-microsecond layer on. The on-die engine widens that lead at every point, recovering up to 37.3 percentage points over the deployed static placement, while adding 0.02% of a current accelerator's transistors.
original_abstract.source_title: A Per-Step Load-Balancing Engine for Expert-Parallel MoE Serving

en.text: Relief balances token assignments across replicated experts at every decoding step. A pairwise integer-halving relaxation avoids solving an expensive optimization problem online, and the paper evaluates GPU, FPGA and on-die implementations. Its reported utilization improvements concern expert-parallel execution and should not be equated with end-to-end throughput gains. The method offers a hardware-oriented approach to per-step load balancing that could be tested in sparse recommendation serving.

zh.text: Relief 在每个解码步骤重新平衡复制专家之间的 token 分配，用成对整数减半的松弛方法减少在线求解开销，并评估 GPU、FPGA 和片上实现。论文报告的利用率改善针对专家并行执行，不能直接当作端到端吞吐提升。它为稀疏推荐服务提供了逐步负载均衡的硬件实现思路。

original_abstract.text: Language-model agents increasingly run on workstations with a few consumer GPUs, where large mixture-of-experts (MoE) models keep part of their experts in host memory. With existing CPU-GPU engines, these agents get fast prefill or fast decode, not both: this http URL's expert cache skips forward passes of more than 32 tokens to keep the experts of decode cached, so an agent waits 2.1-2.8 s after each tool output, whereas its default layer placement shortens this wait but is 1.5-1.6$\times$ slower in decode. Our key insight is that a short prefill touches too many distinct experts to upload, yet sends 84% of its expert activations (routes) to a stable set of experts that fits in GPU memory. We present Ostinato, a CPU-GPU MoE inference engine that computes these experts on the GPUs in every forward pass without changing what the model computes. Short prefills split their routes, leaving fewer than one of a token's six routed experts per layer to the CPU; long prefills upload each distinct cold expert once; and each decode step runs as one fixed-shape CUDA graph per GPU. On real coding and customer-service agent sessions with DeepSeek-V4-Flash on four RTX 4090D GPUs, Ostinato is the fastest engine in both phases and finishes every session sooner than all six baselines. Against this http URL and KTransformers, it cuts the median wait after a tool output by 22-55% and finishes sessions 1.4-2.5$\times$ sooner.
original_abstract.source_title: Ostinato: Fast CPU-GPU MoE Inference for Local Agents via Resident Experts in Every Forward Pass

en.text: Ostinato keeps frequently used experts resident on GPUs while offloading other MoE work to CPUs. It adapts execution to short and long prefills and uses fixed CUDA graphs for decoding. DeepSeek-V4-Flash agent-session experiments on four RTX 4090D GPUs report shorter waits after tool outputs and faster session completion than evaluated CPU-GPU baselines, without changing model outputs. The execution design may inform limited-memory sparse recommendation deployments, although recommendation workloads were not studied.

zh.text: Ostinato 让常用专家驻留 GPU，其余 MoE 计算由 CPU 协作承担；它分别处理短、长预填充，并用固定 CUDA 图执行解码。在四张 RTX 4090D 上运行 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 的智能体会话实验中，相比所测 CPU–GPU 基线，工具返回后的等待和会话完成时间缩短，模型输出保持不变。这种执行方式可供显存受限的稀疏推荐部署参考，尚未验证推荐负载。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation models represent items as sequences of discrete tokens known as semantic IDs. Existing approaches derive these identifiers using residual or hierarchical vector quantization, assuming that tokens carry independent semantic meaning across quantization levels. Revisiting this assumption, we argue that semantic IDs should behave as hierarchical paths where each token's meaning is conditioned on its prefix. This highlights a mismatch between conventional fixed-codebook quantization and the hierarchical structure implicitly learned by generative recommenders. Motivated by this insight, we propose Adaptive Silhouette Tree (AST), a top-down divisive clustering method that constructs semantic IDs as paths within a tree structure. Unlike prior methods with fixed branching factors, AST dynamically determines the number of branches at each node by maximizing the silhouette coefficient, enabling finer partitions in dense regions and compact groupings in homogeneous ones. We further introduce constrained variants that enforce minimum probability mass during splitting to improve supervision for long-tail items. Extensive experiments on five Amazon Review datasets of varying sizes and domains show that AST significantly outperforms strong baselines. These results demonstrate that aligning semantic ID construction with the inherent hierarchical structure of generative recommenders leads to more effective recommendations.
original_abstract.source_title: Not All Branches Are Equal: Adaptive Semantic ID Construction for Generative Recommendation

en.text: Adaptive Silhouette Tree constructs semantic IDs as hierarchical paths whose tokens depend on their prefixes. Instead of a fixed branching factor, top-down clustering selects each node’s branching count using the silhouette coefficient; constrained variants maintain minimum probability mass to strengthen long-tail supervision. The authors report improvements over strong baselines on five Amazon Review datasets. The transferable design insight is to adapt identifier capacity to local item structure before scaling a generative recommender, rather than assume fixed-codebook quantization matches every region of the catalog.

zh.text: Adaptive Silhouette Tree 将语义 ID 构造成逐层路径，让每个词元的含义依赖此前的前缀。自顶向下聚类依据轮廓系数选择各节点的分支数量，而非固定分叉数；受约束版本还要求分支具有最小概率质量，改善长尾监督。作者在五个 Amazon Review 数据集上报告优于较强基线。对生成式推荐可借鉴的是先让标识容量适应商品空间的局部结构，再扩展模型，而不假设固定码本划分适合所有区域。

original_abstract.text: User sequence modeling is widely used in recommendation and advertising. Search ranking presents an additional challenge: the current query expresses immediate intent, while a candidate product determines which parts of a user's long-term history are relevant. We present a production sequence framework for sponsored-product ranking that augments recent behavior with two retrieval channels over long-term history: candidate-nearest-neighbor retrieval and query-nearest-neighbor retrieval. The selected actions are encoded together with dedicated query and candidate context tokens, while candidate-aware early fusion injects the candidate into every history token. Offline ablations show that dual retrieval improves major ranking metrics relative to the production baseline. In an online A/B test on sponsored-product search traffic, the model increased CTR, attributed conversion rate, and orders per impression.
original_abstract.source_title: Query- and Candidate-Aware Long User Sequence Modeling for Sponsored Product Ranking in Search

en.text: This sponsored-product ranking framework supplements recent actions with long-term history retrieved through two channels: nearest neighbors of the current query and of the candidate product. Dedicated query/candidate tokens and candidate-aware early fusion condition the selected behavior sequence. Offline ablations improve ranking metrics over the production baseline, and an online A/B test increases CTR, attributed conversion rate and orders per impression. It offers a practical way to select relevant portions of long histories before applying a more expressive ranking model.

zh.text: 这项商品广告排序方法用两条检索通道补充近期行为：分别寻找与当前查询、候选商品相近的长期历史。选出的行为与专用查询、候选词元一起编码，并在早期融合阶段把候选信息注入每个历史词元。离线消融优于生产基线，线上 A/B 测试提升 CTR、归因转化率和每次曝光订单数。它为长历史提供了实用的相关片段选择方法，再由表达能力更强的排序模型处理这些片段。

original_abstract.text: Energy claims for efficient neural networks are often inferred from operation counts. We report direct GPU energy measurements on two workloads that batch very differently, recurrent policies in GPU-vectorised multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) and mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models, and ask one question of both: can the rows of a batch be made to share computation, across the batch and over time, at a measured saving? On recurrent policies the answer so far is no. Shared activity patterns exist but rarely last one step, masking a frozen policy fails, and trained-in masks succeed only because a fixed mask is equivalent to a narrow GRU, at 11x the energy of a small dense policy in our implementation. Test-time steering adds nothing beyond re-picking on either workload. On MoE models the answer is yes, and granularity decides how much: on Qwen3-30B-A3B, batch-aware routing reads 25-31% fewer expert weights within KL 0.05, with benchmark changes within noise at 500 items, and uses 12-18% less energy per token on a fused forward. We also introduce persistence-aware OEA, a one-parameter rule that keeps the batch-aware cut with about 40% fewer new experts per step than native routing at batch 32-64, though its energy has not yet been measured. These are pilot measurements on one GPU type, and we state their limits.
original_abstract.source_title: Direct GPU Energy Measurements of Batch-Level Sharing in Mixture-of-Experts and Recurrent Models

en.text: The paper measures GPU energy directly when batch rows share computation in recurrent policies and MoE language models. Recurrent-policy masking does not produce savings in the evaluated implementation. For Qwen3-30B-A3B, batch-aware routing reads fewer expert weights and lowers energy per token by 12–18% in a fused forward pass, with benchmark changes within noise on 500 items. A persistence-aware rule reduces expert churn but has no energy measurement yet. These single-GPU-type pilot results motivate measuring energy rather than inferring savings from operation counts.

zh.text: 论文直接测量批内共享计算的 GPU 能耗，分别考察循环策略模型和 MoE 语言模型。所测实现中的循环策略掩码没有节能；Qwen3-30B-A3B 的批感知路由减少专家权重读取，在融合前向中每 token 能耗降低 12%–18%，500 个样本上的基准变化处于噪声范围。另一个持续性感知规则减少专家切换，但尚未测量其能耗。这些单一 GPU 类型上的初步结果提示，扩模效率应直接测量，不能只靠运算量推算。

original_abstract.text: LLM inference has two phases with different bottlenecks: LLM prefill runs once per request and is compute-intensive. Decoding repeats for every output token and is limited by memory bandwidth. To address the challenges associated with this issue, different solutions have been proposed. All of these solutions use the same model for both prefill and decode phases. We propose BridgeKV, which uses a larger model for prefill and a smaller model of the same family for decoding. A lightweight KV-stitching module translates the larger model's prompt cache into the smaller model's cache layout. It handles differences in cache shape and representation through learned local layer mixing and separate nonlinear maps for keys and values. With both models frozen, we train the module to align their caches and make the smaller model follow the larger model's next-token predictions. A second training stage adds low-rank adapters when further task adaptation is needed. Across six model pairs and five datasets, BridgeKV outperforms fine-tuned small-model baselines with matched trainable parameter budgets in all 30 settings. It closes up to 80% of the quality gap to using the larger model for both phases. On one A40 GPU, Llama-3.1-Instruct-8B to Llama-3.2-Instruct-1B achieves 3.0X faster requests than the larger model alone, with latency close to the smaller model alone. BridgeKV can improve the hardware and system solutions that separate prefill and decode phases across GPUs. A separate serving simulation models request arrivals, queues, and cache transfer. For Llama-3.1-Instruct-70B to Llama-3.2-Instruct-1B, it predicts up to 33.86X faster requests and 27.5X lower energy use than using the larger model for both prefill and decode phases.
original_abstract.source_title: BridgeKV: Large-Model Prefill and Small-Model Decoding for LLM Inference via KV Cache Translation

en.text: BridgeKV uses a large model for prompt prefill and a smaller model from the same family for decoding. A learned cache adapter mixes nearby layers and separately maps keys and values while both base models remain frozen; an optional second stage adds low-rank adapters. Across six model pairs and five datasets it beats matched-trainable-budget small-model baselines. A single-A40 experiment reports a threefold request speedup over the large model; larger gains come from simulation. The approach offers a quality-cost tradeoff to investigate for generative recommendation.

zh.text: BridgeKV 用大模型处理提示词预填充，再让同系列小模型逐 token 解码。缓存适配器学习相邻层混合及键、值的独立映射，基础模型保持冻结，后续可增加低秩适配。在六组模型、五个数据集上，它优于可训练参数预算匹配的小模型基线。单张 A40 实验相对大模型报告约三倍请求加速，更大的收益数字来自模拟。该方法为生成式推荐提供了质量与成本权衡的研究方向。

original_abstract.text:
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference with expert parallelism (EP) relies on All-to-All communication, making computation-communication overlap strategies critical for achieving high performance. However, no strategy is universally optimal. Across 103 production configurations, varying input lengths, and four hardware platforms, we observe that the fastest strategy shifts based on model shape, EP degree, input length, and hardware. Since no strategy dominates more than 80.6% of configurations, configuration-aware selection is necessary.
In this work, we propose OverlapAdvisor, which models overlap stages using two granularities to capture computation-communication dependencies. OverlapAdvisor builds a unified performance model, accounting for deviations from peak compute, memory, and communication performance across workloads and hardware. This model enables launch-time, configuration-aware strategy selection within two serving engines. We conduct experiments on four MoE models (30B-235B) against three baselines, utilizing SGLang and vLLM. At the kernel level, OverlapAdvisor achieves 1.16x average and 1.59x maximum speedups, with a prediction MAPE of 3.3%-15.9%. In SGLang and vLLM, it improves end-to-end throughput up to 31.7%. Its granularity-guided optimizations further achieve median speedups of 1.10x for DeepEP-v1 and 1.22x for FlashMoE.
original_abstract.source_title: OverlapAdvisor: Modeling and Adapting Computation-Communication Overlap for Distributed MoE Serving

en.text: OverlapAdvisor models compute-communication dependencies at two granularities to select an overlap strategy for expert-parallel MoE serving. The preferred strategy changes with model shape, expert-parallel degree, input length and hardware, so selection happens at engine launch rather than relying on one fixed strategy. Tests of four 30B-235B models on four platforms report up to 31.7% end-to-end throughput improvement in SGLang and vLLM. This is a useful systems design for distributed sparse recommendation, with transfer gains still unmeasured.

zh.text: OverlapAdvisor 用两种粒度建模计算与通信依赖，在引擎启动时为专家并行 MoE 选择重叠策略。最佳策略会随模型形状、专家并行度、输入长度和硬件改变，不能固定使用同一方案。论文在四个平台、四个 300 亿至 2350 亿参数模型上测试，SGLang 和 vLLM 的端到端吞吐提升最高为 31.7%。这种按配置选择策略的设计可供分布式稀疏推荐参考，迁移收益尚未测量。

original_abstract.text: A model that takes over another model's conversation must normally re-read the whole history; a text hand-off shortens the re-read only by dropping content. KV-cache translation instead maps the source's cache into the target's own format, so the target continues from the full context without re-reading it. It works for grouped-query attention (GQA), but open-weights frontier models now cache compressed latents (MLA), sparse-attention indexer keys and fixed-size linear-attention states. We replicate KV-Lingo on a GQA pair and then give, for each of these objects, where to capture and inject it and a mechanism that reaches native quality. We study two hybrid pairs at 16-48B scale in both directions, Kimi-VL-A3B - Kimi-Linear-48B (MLA - MLA + Kimi Delta Attention) and Qwen3.5-27B - Qwen3.8-27B (Gated DeltaNet hybrids), plus a sparse-attention target (Qwen3.8-27B - Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). MLA latents translate with token-wise linear maps; recurrent states are copied with a closed-form correction or synthesised by replaying the target's own recurrence. Exact long-range recall needs token identity: decoding token ids from the source's layer-0 MLA latent raises needle recall from 0.09 to 0.99 at 2-32K and to 0.83-1.00 at 64K, eight times the longest training prompt. The hybrid full-MLA direction is within the paired confidence interval of native quality on every task metric, and same-shape GDN hybrids reach the native level in both directions (apart from 6% refusals inherited from the source), with time to first token 18.7 and 46.8 times shorter than a re-read at 64K tokens. Segment-wise multi-turn transfer stays at the re-prefill level; naive re-translation collapses. On the sparse-attention target, predicted indexer keys recall the needle as well as the target's own keys (one seed). We state as a hypothesis how the recipes transfer to 300B+ hybrid flagships.
original_abstract.source_title: Translating KV Caches Between Hybrid-Attention Language Models: MLA Latents, Linear-Attention States and Sparse-Attention Indexers

en.text: This work translates cached context across hybrid language models, covering compressed attention latents, recurrent states and sparse-attention indexer keys. Linear maps handle some latent caches, while recurrent transfer uses correction or replay of the target recurrence; exact long-range recall also requires token identity. Experiments on 16–48B hybrid pairs examine quality and time to first token, and segment-wise transfer avoids failures of naive repeated translation. The recipes may inform model switching over shared user histories; extension to 300B-plus models is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated result.

zh.text: 这项工作研究混合注意力模型之间的上下文缓存转换，覆盖压缩注意力表示、循环状态和稀疏索引键。部分缓存可用线性映射转换，循环状态则需要校正或重放目标模型递推；精确远距离回忆还依赖 token 身份。16–48B 模型对的实验考察质量和首 token 延迟，分段转移避免了简单重复转换的失效。方法可启发共享用户历史上的模型切换，扩展至 300B 以上模型仍是待验证假设。

original_abstract.text: On-demand delivery platforms such as DoorDash and Uber Eats impose a constraint absent in traditional e-commerce: merchants beyond the user's delivery range are invalid candidates rather than merely low-ranked. Generative retrieval has recently shown strong potential in large-scale retrieval systems. Adapting it to this setting, however, poses three challenges. First, existing semantic IDs encode geography only as a soft signal, so reachability can only rely on a non-differentiable post-generation hard truncation. Second, user preferences vary substantially across both regions and queries, so aggregating historical behaviors without conditioning on geography and the current query yields biased interest estimates. Third, the retrieved candidate set is evaluated by its collective value, yet autoregressive training scores each sequence independently, with no set-level signal to discourage redundant near-duplicates. To address the challenges, we propose TS-GEAR, a unified generative retrieval framework for on-demand delivery: (1) Geo-Semantic ID splits merchant identifiers into geographic prefixes and semantic suffixes, making reachability a prediction target rather than a post-hoc filter; (2) Query-Geo Target Attention aggregates historical behaviors using the real-time query and location as dual targets, while encoding each behavior's own location into its attention key; (3) GMPO (Group Marginal Policy Optimization) rewrites advantages using a deduplicated group reward and marginal advantage within GRPO, avoiding auxiliary diversity objectives. Deployed online with a lightweight 0.1B backbone, TS-GEAR serves over 150 million queries per day in the search advertising pipeline of Taobao Shangou, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art generative retrieval methods on both HitRate and geographic validity, and achieving 3.8% gains in ad impressions and 4.2% in ad revenue.
original_abstract.source_title: TS-GEAR: Taobao Shangou GEnerative Ad Retrieval

en.text: TS-GEAR addresses delivery-range validity and set-level value in generative ad retrieval. Geographic prefixes and semantic suffixes make reachability part of the identifier target; query-and-location-conditioned attention selects user-history signals, while group marginal policy optimization discourages redundant candidates through group rewards. The authors report deployment of a 0.1B model on over 150 million daily Taobao Shangou queries, with ad impressions and revenue increasing by 3.8% and 4.2%. It is a concrete industrial recipe for building location constraints and candidate-set value into generative retrieval.

zh.text: TS-GEAR 面向配送范围受限的生成式广告召回：用地理前缀与语义后缀编码商家，让可配送性进入预测目标；用查询和位置共同引导历史行为注意力，再以组级奖励和边际优势减少候选重复。作者报告 0.1B 模型已在淘宝闪购承接每日超过 1.5 亿查询，广告曝光和收入分别提升 3.8% 与 4.2%。它为工业生成式召回提供了将地理约束、候选集合价值接入模型训练的方法。

original_abstract.text: Mixture-of-Experts language models are cheap to run per token but expensive to hold in GPU memory, which drives the cost of serving them in production. One-shot expert compression shrinks them after a single calibration pass. Its two current state-of-the-art methods are REAP for expert pruning, which deletes the least salient experts, and REAM for expert merging, which merges them into the most salient ones. Both have been evaluated only on academic benchmarks. We compare the two on five multilingual production tasks of a web-hosting company, from classification to the generation of marketing HTML email templates, with two 30B-parameter models (Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 and the hybrid Mamba-attention Nemotron-3.5-Lightning) at 25% and 50% of experts removed and the same calibration data. Pruning wins: on the same rows, REAP is significantly better in 16 of 20 comparisons and REAM in 2. At 25%, REAP keeps 93.6% of Qwen3-30B's generative quality and REAM 62.5%, although on benchmarks the two are within a point for the same model. The damage concentrates in the output contract rather than the content: 89.8-95.2% of each significant loss on email templates comes from hard-gate failures such as invalid JSON, broken mobile layouts and runaway generation, and most failed non-English domain descriptions copy the prompt's English opening phrase. Cross-perplexity and logit divergence, two diagnostics from the REAP paper, also track production quality, as does the rate of repetition loops; n-gram diversity does not. We close with practical guidance for compressing MoE models for production.
original_abstract.source_title: Prune, Don't Merge: Expert Compression of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs on Multilingual Production Tasks

en.text: The study compares expert pruning and merging on five multilingual production tasks using two 30B MoE models, matched calibration data, and 25% or 50% expert removal. Pruning is significantly better in 16 of 20 comparisons, while merging wins in two. Much of the observed generative degradation comes from output-contract failures such as invalid JSON and broken layouts, which academic scores can conceal. The practical lesson for compressing sparse recommenders is to validate the downstream output contract as well as quality; recommendation workloads were not tested.

zh.text: 论文用两款 30B MoE 模型，在相同校准数据、移除 25% 或 50% 专家的条件下，对比五类多语言生产任务中的专家裁剪与合并。20 组比较中，裁剪显著更好有 16 组，合并更好有两组。生成质量损失大量来自 JSON 无效、布局破坏等输出格式问题，学术基准分数可能掩盖这些缺陷。压缩稀疏推荐模型时也应验证下游接口约束，但论文没有测试推荐负载。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation (GR) is moving industrial recommender systems (RecSys) from scoring candidate items to autoregressively generating item identifiers. This shift promises higher recommendation quality, but makes serving substantially harder: each request executes a short sequence of dependent decoding steps that explore a large item space and select promising candidates on the latency-critical path. GR not only creates structural mismatches with conventional RecSys pipelines, but also challenges the architectural and optimization assumptions of LLM serving stacks, making direct adoption of existing systems difficult. We present RecoGEM, our production GR serving system. RecoGEM uses a runtime--engine decoupling architecture to move GR-specific serving responsibilities, such as candidate-state transitions and live artifact updates, to a dedicated runtime. Its execution engine exploits GR's short token sequences, large candidate populations, and predictable step shapes to optimize self-attention, candidate selection, and execution planning. RecoGEM has been deployed for over nine months across our production lines, serving applications with hundreds of millions of users and supporting more than ten GR model families. On our OneModel production workloads, RecoGEM reaches over 1,000 QPS per serving instance with P99 latency below 35 ms and a 2.88$\times$ throughput improvement over representative baselines.
original_abstract.source_title: RecoGEM: A Serving System for Production-Scale Generative Recommendation

en.text: RecoGEM separates a generative-recommendation runtime, which manages candidate transitions and live artifact updates, from an execution engine optimized for short decoding sequences, large candidate sets and predictable step shapes. The authors report more than nine months of production deployment across over ten model families. On OneModel workloads, a serving instance exceeds 1,000 QPS with P99 latency below 35 ms and 2.88× the throughput of representative baselines. It offers a concrete systems design for scaling generative recommendation without assuming that conventional ranking or LLM serving stacks fit its workload.

zh.text: RecoGEM 将候选状态转移、在线产物更新交给专用运行时，执行引擎则针对生成式推荐的短解码序列、大候选集合和较稳定的步骤形状优化注意力、候选选择与执行计划。作者报告系统已生产部署超过九个月、支持十余类模型；在 OneModel 工作负载上，单实例超过 1,000 QPS，P99 延迟低于 35 毫秒，吞吐量为代表性基线的 2.88 倍。它展示了生成式推荐扩展服务能力时，如何围绕自身负载特点设计执行系统。

original_abstract.text: Dual-batch overlap (DBO) hides mixture-of-experts (MoE) communication behind another microbatch's computation, but only after dispatch send releases the GPU. The time dispatch send holds the GPU therefore stays exposed, while network progress after release can be hidden. We evaluate GPUDirect Async - Kernel Initiated (GDA-KI) Free Flow, an NCCL-EP research configuration that leaves WQE construction on the GPU but moves send progression to a host thread. On a GB300 NVL72 system, GDA-KI Free Flow reduces dispatch-send time relative to default GDA-KI at every operating point in the evaluated parameter sweep. An experiment that inserts a GPU delay between dispatch send and receive shows that offload increases the in-flight interval. Depending on the load, 32-96 microseconds of computation or other independent work between send and receive hides the deferred progress, leaving less exposed time than default GDA-KI. In disaggregated vLLM serving with DBO, GDA-KI Free Flow lowers median TPOT by 15-25% relative to NCCL-EP default GDA-KI and by 16-42% relative to DeepEP v1.
original_abstract.source_title: Release Sooner, Expose Less: Offloading MoE Dispatch in NCCL-EP under Dual-Batch Overlap

en.text: The revised paper evaluates GDA-KI Free Flow, an NCCL-EP configuration that keeps construction of work-queue entries on the GPU but moves send progression to a host thread. Releasing GPU resources earlier lets another microbatch’s computation hide deferred communication. GB300 NVL72 tests report that 32–96 microseconds of independent work can hide that progress; disaggregated vLLM experiments lower median time per output token by 15–25% versus default GDA-KI and 16–42% versus DeepEP v1. The technique may inform sparse recommendation serving, but results remain tied to the evaluated hardware and workloads.

zh.text: 修订版集中评估 GDA-KI Free Flow：GPU 仍负责构建工作队列项，发送推进则移到主机线程，让 GPU 更早释放资源，用另一微批次计算覆盖延后的通信。GB300 NVL72 测试中，32–96 微秒独立工作可隐藏这部分推进；分离式 vLLM 实验的输出 token 中位耗时比默认 GDA-KI 低 15%–25%，比 DeepEP v1 低 16%–42%。该技术可供稀疏推荐服务参考，结果仍受所测硬件和负载限制。

original_abstract.text: Post-LayerNorm Transformers have seen limited practical adoption due to enduring difficulties in scaling them to large depths. While prior research has focused on stabilising Post-LayerNorm by improving conditioning at initialisation, stability often deteriorates when models are trained with large learning rates, forcing additional compromises. In the decoder-only settings we study, existing Post-LayerNorm methods fail to outperform strong Pre-LayerNorm baselines. We propose KiteNorm, a post-norm training method designed to break this trend by constraining hidden-state variance. This approach is motivated by a bound on the LayerNorm Jacobian suggesting that variance growth contributes to gradient vanishing, alongside empirical evidence linking it to rank collapse. KiteNorm combines residual scaling and variance regularisation to maintain stability throughout training, supported by scalarised double-normalisation that provides separately learnable scales for the skip and residual branches. Across decoder-only Transformers up to 1.3B parameters, KiteNorm improves training stability and outperforms leading baselines at their optimal learning rates, with scaling laws favouring KiteNorm across depth, width, batch size, and training budget. Ablations show that each component is necessary for the full stability and performance gains.
original_abstract.source_title: KiteNorm: Variance Regularisation for Stable and Scalable Post-LN Transformers

en.text: KiteNorm addresses the difficulty of scaling Post-LayerNorm Transformers by controlling hidden-state variance throughout training. It combines residual scaling, variance regularization and separately learnable scales for skip and residual branches. Experiments on decoder-only models up to 1.3B parameters report improved stability and favorable scaling across depth, width, batch size and training budget. This offers a concrete normalization recipe to investigate in deeper CTR architectures; recommendation gains have not been established.

zh.text: KiteNorm 通过约束隐藏状态方差，改善 Post-LayerNorm Transformer 随深度增加而出现的训练不稳定。方法结合残差缩放、方差正则，以及跳连和残差分支各自可学习的尺度。在最高 13 亿参数的解码器模型上，论文报告了稳定性改善，并比较了深度、宽度、批量和训练预算的扩展趋势。它可为更深的 CTR 架构提供归一化方案，但尚未验证推荐任务收益。

original_abstract.text: Low-precision pretraining is usually judged by validation loss. We ask whether matching loss also means learning rare facts as efficiently. We train transformers from scratch with emulated 4-bit matrix multiplications on synthetic biographies with controlled exposure counts, on their own and mixed into web text. NVFP4 needs 1.32$\times$ and 1.52$\times$ as many exposures as BF16 to match its recall while validation loss differs by only 0.5% and 2%, and 1.26$\times$ and 1.30$\times$ when both models are evaluated with BF16 matrix multiplications. Under our primary readout, the exposure cost is about 1.2$\times$ at matched loss. Zero-mean gradient noise reproduces the cost of quantizing only the backward pass, which barely moves the loss. In a controlled experiment at twice the NVFP4 error, noise fed only to Adam's second-moment estimate acts like a lower learning rate and its cost fades, whereas noise in the update lowers its signal-to-noise ratio and carries about two thirds of the cost through the end of training. Raising the learning rate to offset the smaller average step does not recover the cost, either for this noise or for NVFP4. Gradient statistics of BF16 checkpoints rank the costs of formats, partial quantizations and noise controls without fitting (Spearman 0.96). We suggest measuring rare-fact acquisition alongside loss when evaluating low-precision recipes.
original_abstract.source_title: What the Loss Curve Misses: FP4 Pretraining Slows the Acquisition of Rare Facts

en.text: This study asks whether similar validation loss guarantees similar rare-fact acquisition under low-precision pretraining. Transformers trained with emulated FP4 matrix operations on controlled synthetic biographies require more exposures to match BF16 recall, including when mixed with web text. Gradient-noise controls link much of the cost to reduced update signal-to-noise rather than merely smaller average steps. The findings motivate evaluating long-tail learning separately from aggregate loss when scaling low-precision recommendation training; the evidence is synthetic language-model learning, not recommendation.

zh.text: 这项研究检查：低精度预训练的验证损失接近，是否意味着稀有事实也能以同样速度学会。在可控合成人物资料及其与网页文本的混合实验中，使用仿真 FP4 矩阵运算的 Transformer 需要更多重复曝光才能达到 BF16 的记忆水平。梯度噪声对照把较多代价归因于更新信噪比降低，而不只是平均步长变小。它提醒低精度推荐训练单独评估长尾学习，不只看总体损失；现有证据来自合成语言模型任务。

original_abstract.text: DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) reduces the computational cost of attention through token-level selection. However, its indexer still scores the entire causal prefix for each query, making indexing a dominant source of latency in long-context inference. Notably, the indexer alone can account for more than 50% of total prefill GPU time at long context lengths. To address this bottleneck, we propose ADIndex, an Adaptive and Distillation-driven Indexing method for token-level sparse attention. ADIndex integrates three key components: (i) a layer-wise calibration strategy that adaptively accommodates cross-query retrieval overlap, motivated by our observation of pronounced inter-layer heterogeneity; (ii) a group-level distillation scheme that leverages this heterogeneity to efficiently train adaptive layer-wise group indexers, capturing salient retrieval signals from individual queries; and (iii) a low-latency inference strategy that reduces repeated full-prefix scans through token bank sharing within query groups while retaining query-specific refinement. Experiments on DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.1 demonstrate that ADIndex preserves near-lossless task performance on LongBench, LongBench v2, and RULER while delivering substantial efficiency gains over standard DSA, including prefill and decoding kernel speedups of up to 6.22x and 3.40x, respectively, at a context length of 256K across the layer-wise reuse configurations, as well as an end-to-end serving speedup of 1.54x at a context length of 128K.
original_abstract.source_title: ADIndex: Layer-Adaptive Sparse Attention Indexing via Group-Level Distillation

en.text: ADIndex reduces sparse-attention indexing cost by calibrating query overlap per layer, distilling group-level indexers and sharing candidate token banks with query-specific refinement. Experiments on DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.1 evaluate long-context quality and serving speed. Kernel acceleration is larger than the reported end-to-end improvement, so the two should be distinguished. Sharing indexing work may help long-sequence generative recommendation, but its recommendation accuracy and serving benefit have not been tested.

zh.text: ADIndex 先校准各层查询对历史位置的重合程度，再蒸馏分组索引器，共享候选 token 集合并按查询细化，减少稀疏注意力的索引开销。论文在 DeepSeek-V3.2 和 GLM-5.1 上评估长上下文质量与服务速度，内核加速幅度大于端到端收益。共享索引计算可供长序列生成式推荐借鉴，推荐准确率和实际服务收益仍需测试。

original_abstract.text: Banks now train foundation models on ordered sequences of customer events such as transactions, app sessions, and authorizations. Deployed, such a model predicts forward in time, often for customers and merchants absent from training, yet each is evaluated on private data, so no two can be compared. Public benchmarks for such sequences rarely test a period the model has not seen; recommendation studies usually hold out each user's last events instead. We present INTENT (INTEraction, Novelty, and Transfer evaluation for next-action prediction), a public benchmark that scores a model in seven cells defined by whether the user, the period, and the target item appeared in training. An audit of 59 public dataset families retains five datasets; the most common defect is the lack of a calendar timestamp that orders events. No date lies within the time span of all five datasets, so each is split at its own cutoff, chosen by one rule fixed before any model is evaluated. Summed over the datasets, every cell holds at least 111,769 users. In reference results the cell determines the best model: a transformer leads on seen items after the cutoff but scores zero on new items, a variant that embeds item metadata helps mainly on MicroLens, and repeating the user's last item leads on new items in four of five datasets. This parameter-free control also shows that on three datasets most of the score lost after the cutoff reflects changed behavior rather than the model. The pipeline, the cutoff rule, and the per-cell user counts are publicly available.
original_abstract.source_title: INTENT: Out-of-Sample, Out-of-Time, and Cold-Start Evaluation on User Event Sequences

en.text: INTENT evaluates next-action models across seven cells separating seen and unseen users, past and future periods, and seen and new target items. It audits 59 public dataset families and retains five with usable global timelines and sufficient coverage. Reference results change substantially by cell: a transformer leads on seen future items but fails on new items, where repeating the last item wins on four datasets. The benchmark helps distinguish sequence-model scaling from split artifacts and changes in user behavior.

zh.text: INTENT 将下一行为预测划分为七种测试情形，分别区分已见与新用户、过去与未来时段、已见与新目标商品。它审查 59 个公开数据集系列，保留五个具备可用全局时间线和足够覆盖的数据集。不同情形下模型排名明显变化：Transformer 在未来已见商品上领先，却无法预测新商品；重复上一商品的简单方法在四个数据集的新商品测试中领先。这有助于区分序列扩模收益、数据切分影响和用户行为变化。

original_abstract.text: Expert parallelism (EP) shards the experts of a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layer across GPUs, so every MoE layer requires two all-to-all communications, namely dispatch and combine. Compared with training, inference processes relatively few tokens per GPU at a time, and at small batch sizes fixed costs that do not grow with the number of tokens, rather than data movement, dominate the latency. We present NVLinkOneSided, a one-sided EP all-to-all for GPUs within a single NVLink domain. Each source rank pushes its tokens, without first exchanging metadata, into rank-major buffers on the target GPUs, and the grouped GEMMs read them in place instead of from a per-expert copy. We provide two protocols for the synchronization that the communication requires, namely Fence and Sentinel, for high-throughput and low-latency scenarios respectively. On Blackwell GPUs, NVLinkOneSided completes dispatch and combine 1.2-3.0$\times$ faster than DeepEP, with the largest speedups at small batch sizes. The resulting MoE layer is up to 2.4$\times$ faster than DeepEP with DeepGEMM. It even outperforms the fused DeepGEMM MegaMoE at up to 128 tokens per GPU, making it still competitive for decoding. We expose NVLinkOneSided through a modular interface, so that it is agnostic to the activation quantization format, decoupled from the MoE compute backend and easy to integrate into inference frameworks.
original_abstract.source_title: One-Sided Expert-Parallel All-to-All for Mixture-of-Experts Inference over NVLink

en.text: NVLinkOneSided sends routed tokens directly into buffers organized by source rank and lets grouped matrix multiplication consume them in place. This removes metadata exchange and extra copies before expert computation. Separate synchronization modes target throughput and latency. Blackwell experiments report faster dispatch, combine and MoE-layer execution than evaluated baselines, especially for small batches. The idea is relevant to sparse recommendation serving, but its gains depend on the NVLink hardware and routing workload.

zh.text: NVLinkOneSided 将路由后的 token 直接写入按来源节点组织的缓冲区，让专家矩阵乘法原地读取，省去元数据交换和额外搬运。两种同步方式分别面向吞吐与延迟。Blackwell 实验显示，分发、合并及 MoE 层执行快于所测基线，小批量下尤为明显。它可启发稀疏推荐服务优化，收益取决于 NVLink 硬件和路由负载。

original_abstract.text: Serving large language models at high concurrency with long contexts requires KV-cache capacity and attention bandwidth that grow with the decode pool. Existing parallelization strategies trade one against the other: data parallelism replicates model weights, limiting KV capacity; tensor parallelism stops scaling attention at the model's KV-head count and pushes dense collectives across nodes; and decode context parallelism (DCP) recovers capacity by sharding the sequence but adds cross-node aggregation of partial attention results. We observe that during decode, dense layers and attention scale differently: dense layers amortize weight reads across the batch and run efficiently within a single NVLink domain, whereas attention cost grows with every active request's KV cache. We present Decode Token Parallelism (TKNP), a decode-pool architecture that decouples weight placement from attention ownership. TKNP distributes a single model copy across nodes in balanced layer blocks. The active node holding a block executes its projections and MLP for the full batch using intra-node tensor parallelism, while every node computes attention for its own requests against locally resident KV cache. This extends request-local attention across nodes without replicating weights: only current-token activations cross the network, dense all-reduces remain within NVLink, and attention requires no cross-node merging of partial results. Implemented in vLLM and evaluated on Llama 3.1 405B and Nemotron-4 340B on up to 64 H100 GPUs, TKNP improves completion throughput for long-context, high-concurrency workloads by up to 1.7$\times$ over DCP and by up to 2.06$\times$ over data parallelism at matched GPU count.
original_abstract.source_title: Decode Token Parallelism: Memory-Efficient Distributed Attention Parallelism for Scalable LLM Decoding

en.text: Decode Token Parallelism separates model-weight placement from request-specific attention and key-value cache ownership. Layers are balanced across nodes, while each request’s attention and cache stay local; only token activations cross nodes. Experiments on Llama-3.1-405B and Nemotron-4-340B use up to 64 H100 GPUs and compare completion throughput at matched GPU counts. Local cache ownership may inform large generative recommenders, although the reported gains are from language-model serving.

zh.text: Decode Token Parallelism 将模型权重放置与请求的注意力、键值缓存归属分开：各节点分担模型层，每个请求的注意力和缓存留在本地，跨节点只传递 token 激活。实验使用最多 64 张 H100，在相同 GPU 数量下比较 Llama-3.1-405B 和 Nemotron-4-340B 的完成吞吐。缓存就地处理可供大型生成式推荐服务参考，现有收益来自语言模型负载。

original_abstract.text: Looped language models deepen computation without adding parameters, yet caching full-context key-value (KV) states across layers and rounds severely bounds serving batch size. We design a looped causal encoder-decoder (CED) that achieves recurrent depth with zero round-wise KV growth, addressing where and how to loop an asymmetric stack in which only sparse encoder layers generate global KV. We find that recurrence must be placed in the encoder to iteratively refine global KV representations rather than re-reading static decoder projections, which both drives language-modeling gains and preserves long-context scaling. Furthermore, training the encoder loop under stochastic recurrence depth induces a fixed-point equilibrium where every round losslessly shares the last round's KV cache. Compounding cross-layer and cross-round KV sharing, the resulting Looped CED matches an unlooped CED's minimal memory footprint and recovers 86-93% of a looped Transformer's gain with 1/6 of its global KV. To test serving at production scale, we loop the 552B-parameter DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash for 8 rounds on one 4xGB200 node: with per-layer and per-round KV the loop cannot fit a single 128K-token request, whereas Looped CED holds 36.8x less KV per token, fits 38 such requests (as many as the unlooped model), and serves 3.6x higher throughput on 8K-token prompts.
original_abstract.source_title: Looping Deeper Without Growing the KV Cache: Recurrent Depth for Causal Encoder-Decoders

en.text: Looped CED places recurrent computation in the encoder of a causal encoder-decoder, where a few layers create the global key-value cache. Stochastic recurrence training allows rounds to share the final round’s cache, avoiding cache growth with recurrent depth. Language-modeling experiments and a DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serving analysis examine the quality-memory tradeoff. The design suggests a way to deepen computation over long histories under a fixed cache budget; recommendation quality remains untested.

zh.text: Looped CED 在因果编码器—解码器的编码端重复计算，由少数层生成全局键值缓存。随机循环深度训练使各轮共享最后一轮缓存，避免缓存随循环次数增长。论文通过语言建模实验和 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 服务分析考察质量与显存的权衡。它为固定缓存预算下增加长历史计算深度提供了思路，推荐效果仍需验证。

original_abstract.text: Classical neural scaling laws model excess risk as a separable power law in model capacity $N$ and dataset size $D$. At finite budgets, however, empirical learning curves and compute-optimal allocations depart from this log-linear frontier. This paper analyzes how spectral and domain heterogeneity govern these finite-scale departures. Along the capacity axis, Mellin--Barnes analysis of covariance resolvents yields a three-term expansion where competing spectral and regularization modes produce finite-scale curvature and logarithmic transitions. Because fitting multiple power laws on narrow pilot grids is ill-conditioned, we eliminate the loss floor via first-order Aitken differencing to obtain a well-conditioned closed-form initializer. Along the data axis, KKT duality reduces $K$-domain mixing to scalar water-filling, yielding finite-budget bottleneck bounds, an online sampling curriculum, and a simplex Hessian metric for cross-domain transfer. Along the iso-compute frontier $C=6ND$, we prove that the optimal allocation exponent drifts in proportion to capacity and data exponent variances, while Schur-complement reduction separates intrinsic drift from frozen-hyperparameter bias. Across 45 operator spectra, Pythia (70M--12B), Chinchilla (245 runs), and RegMix (17 domains), our estimators achieve $5.89\%$ holdout MAPE, cut high-compute allocation regret by up to $76.4\%$, and reduce cross-scale mixture RMSE by $59.4\%$ with zero selection regret.
original_abstract.source_title: Beyond the Log-Linear Frontier: Pre-Asymptotic Analysis of Finite-Budget Neural Scaling Laws

en.text: The paper studies why scaling curves and compute allocations depart from simple power laws at finite budgets. It connects spectral and data-domain heterogeneity to curved learning curves, proposes an initialization method for small pilot grids and derives budget-dependent data mixing and model-data allocation rules. Evaluations use operator spectra and Pythia, Chinchilla and RegMix data. The practical connection to CTR scaling is to check finite-budget curvature before extrapolating from small experiments; the reported fits do not validate these laws for recommendation workloads.

zh.text: 论文研究有限预算下学习曲线和计算分配为何偏离简单幂律，将偏离与谱结构、数据域差异联系起来，并提出适合小规模试验网格的拟合初始化，以及随预算变化的数据混合和模型—数据分配规则。评估使用算子谱及 Pythia、Chinchilla、RegMix 数据。对 CTR 扩模的启发是，外推小实验前先检查有限预算下的曲率；现有拟合结果不代表推荐负载也服从这些规律。

original_abstract.text: Researchers and engineers improve recommendation systems by performing A/B experiments with new model architectures, optimization methods, and data features. However, running full-scale experiments (e.g., full-model training with online data) for every feature change is prohibitively computationally intensive, while the result from a single small-scale experiment is often misleading. To address this challenge, we show that modern recommendation models exhibit feature-invariant scaling: the change of a model's performance follows a predictable scaling-law even when different feature changes are applied to the baseline model. We introduce an efficient method that exploits scaling-laws and uses statistical inference to predict (with confidence intervals) the full-scale effect of an A/B experiment in recommendation systems. This enables practitioners to efficiently filter out neutral or regressive feature changes with only small-scale experimentation. We validate our method on three distinct recommendation model families---Wukong, HSTU, and LLM-based recommendation models---across more than 40 architectural, optimization, and data changes. Our method accurately distinguishes beneficial feature changes from neutral and regressive ones while using only a fraction of the compute required for full-scale evaluation. It also identifies several changes that improve HSTU's state-of-the-art performance on MovieLens-20M. Our results demonstrate that scaling laws can be practically exploited to make compute-efficient decisions for improving industrial-scale recommendation systems.
original_abstract.source_title: Exploiting Feature-invariant Scaling Laws for Efficient A/B Experimentation in Recommendation Systems

en.text: The paper predicts the full-scale effect of a recommendation-model change from several small experiments, with confidence intervals. Its feature-invariant scaling approach covers architecture, optimizer and data changes across Wukong, HSTU and LLM-based recommenders. More than 40 changes are evaluated, enabling neutral or regressive candidates to be filtered at a fraction of full-scale compute. This offers a practical way to allocate experimentation budgets; the reported prediction evidence should not be read as a measured online business lift.

zh.text: 这项工作用多组小规模实验预测推荐模型改动在完整规模下的效果，并给出置信区间。方法利用不同改动下相对效果的扩展规律，覆盖 Wukong、HSTU 和大模型推荐器的架构、优化器及数据变化。论文评估了 40 多项改动，可用较少计算筛掉无效或退化候选，帮助分配扩模实验预算；这些预测结果不等于已验证的线上业务收益。

original_abstract.text: Existing sequential user modeling methods mainly focus on improving the backbone encoder or learning task-specific user representations for a single prediction objective. We instead study how to export the multi-layer user states of a frozen long-history backbone as compact, timestamp-addressable representations for downstream training backfill and serving. In this setting, the user state at a given timestamp summarizes the user's actions before that time, so downstream systems need only the state aligned to each target timestamp rather than the full hidden-state timeline. To this end, we present \texttt{SeqFold}, a compressed-state interface that combines learned multi-channel fusion, channel-specific temporal decay, and Lookup-Free Quantization (LFQ) to produce compact discrete codes from frozen backbone states. Task-specific decoders then map these shared codes into flexible embedding spaces for downstream models. To make timestamp-addressable export practical at scale, we further develop a fused streaming implementation that updates the fusion recurrence after every action while materializing states only at target timestamps. On large-scale proprietary datasets, SeqFold reduces per-state representation storage by $3{,}400\times$ while preserving most of the downstream ranking performance of the uncompressed model, showing that SeqFold is an effective interface for reusing long-history sequence backbones in downstream models.
original_abstract.source_title: SeqFold: Timestamp-Addressable Compressed States for User Action Sequence Backbones

en.text: SeqFold exports compact, timestamp-addressable states from a frozen long-history user backbone. It combines learned channel fusion, channel-specific temporal decay and lookup-free quantization; downstream decoders adapt the shared codes to their own embedding spaces. A fused streaming implementation updates state after every action but materializes it only at requested timestamps. Proprietary-data experiments report 3,400-fold lower per-state storage while preserving most downstream ranking performance. This provides a concrete interface for reusing sequence backbones across training backfill and serving; the storage ratio is not an end-to-end speedup.

zh.text: SeqFold 将冻结的长历史用户骨干状态导出为可按时间戳读取的紧凑表示。它结合多通道融合、各通道的时间衰减和免查表量化，再由下游解码器适配各任务的表示空间。融合流式实现每次行为后都更新状态，只在目标时间戳导出。在私有数据上，每个状态的存储减少约 3,400 倍，同时保留大部分下游排序效果，为训练回填和服务复用序列骨干提供了具体接口；存储压缩比不等于端到端加速比。

original_abstract.text: In Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, the nature of expert specialization remains controversial. Reports of domain-associated expert preferences contrast with analyses attributing routing primarily to token identity or syntactic patterns. To clarify these differing accounts, we look beyond expert-level routing to investigate the neuron-level organization of domain-specialized computation using Routing-Aware Magnitude Profiling (RAMP), a measure developed for this analysis. Using mixed-domain calibration data, we identify domain-specialized neuron sets with 58-74% overlap across multi-source samples of the same domain, compared with 15-24% across domains. To understand how this organization evolves during training, we trace neuron importance throughout pre-training and post-training across three fully open MoE families. Neuron importance continues to reorganize between pre-training checkpoints despite comparatively stable expert-level importance rankings, while post-training largely preserves neuron rankings. Building on these neuron-level perspectives, we further introduce RAMP-based Pruning (RAMPr) to select neurons across experts for balanced multi-domain capability preservation. At 75% neuron retention, RAMPr preserves average 91-98% of original full performance across six models. At 50% retention, our pruning method can reduce resident GPU memory by 36-43% and improves batched prefill throughput by 17-39% effectively. Our code is available at this https URL
original_abstract.source_title: Understanding Mixture-of-Experts Language Models Beyond Expert Boundaries

en.text: RAMP measures neuron contributions weighted by expert routing to study specialization inside MoE models. Domain-associated neuron sets extend across expert boundaries, and neuron rankings can change even when expert rankings remain stable. RAMPr uses this finer view to prune neurons across experts. Evaluations on six models examine quality, resident memory and prefill throughput at different retention levels. Neuron-level capacity allocation could inform sparse recommenders, but no recommendation result is established.

zh.text: RAMP 用专家路由权重加权神经元贡献，观察 MoE 内部的领域分工。相关神经元可以跨越专家边界，专家重要性排名稳定时，内部神经元排名仍可能变化。RAMPr 据此跨专家裁剪神经元，并在六个模型上比较不同保留比例下的质量、常驻显存和预填充吞吐。这种更细粒度的容量分配可供稀疏推荐模型参考，尚无推荐实验结论。

original_abstract.text: Reusing key--value (KV) caches across language model updates could avoid repeated computation of shared context, but changes in model weights raise a fundamental question about what these caches preserve. We investigate direct cache reuse across four model updates, with a detailed study of DeepSeek-V4-Flash to Flash-0731. Our central finding is that caches can retain useful task information without faithfully reproducing the updated model's behavior. Retrieval accuracy varies substantially across updates, ranging from near-native performance to large losses. With source caches already available, reuse achieves median time-to-first-token speedups of $2.10$--$5.08\times$ on three longer-prefix QA benchmarks. To characterize the behavioral differences behind these outcomes, we introduce Functional Cache Divergence, which compares next-token distributions under reused and native caches. Direct KV cache reuse better preserves native model behavior in natural-text continuation, whereas compatibility degrades with increasing prefix length in single-token retrieval tasks. Answer-margin analyses help explain how correct retrieval decisions survive substantial internal state changes. Yet even agreement on the first generated token does not ensure agreement in answer content or stopping behavior. These findings establish task utility and fidelity to native inference as distinct criteria for evaluating cross-version KV cache reuse.
original_abstract.source_title: Can KV Cache Be Reused Across Model Updates? A DeepSeek-V4-Flash Case Study

en.text: This study tests whether an old model’s key-value cache remains useful after a model update. Across four updates, utility and fidelity behave differently: reused caches can reduce time to first token on some question-answering tasks when caches already exist, yet cause large retrieval losses in other settings. Functional Cache Divergence compares next-token distributions to diagnose incompatibility. The work suggests checking cached-history compatibility during model refreshes rather than assuming reuse is safe; recommendation workloads are not evaluated.

zh.text: 论文研究模型更新后能否继续使用旧模型的键值缓存。四次更新的实验表明，可用性与结果一致性并不相同：已有缓存可在部分问答任务中缩短首 token 等待，但在另一些检索设置中造成明显损失。作者用下一 token 分布的差异诊断缓存兼容性。对推荐系统的启发是，更新模型时应检验历史缓存是否仍适用，论文尚未评估推荐负载。
